sentences.text: It has been submitted that petitioner No.1 and opposite party No.2 are husband and wife having been married according to Muslim rites and rituals on 24.10.2021.

After marriage there arose certain matrimonial discord between the parties and due to which opposite party No.2 filed a complaint before Civil Judge (Senior Division)/FTC/ACJM, Balrampur under Section 498A and 323 IPC and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act stating that father of the complainant had given huge amount of dowry at the time of marriage i.e. about Rs.26,00,000/- and immediately thereafter the family of the husband started demand of more dowry i.e. Rs.50 lakhs and due to non-fulfillment of the demands of her in-laws she was regularly physically and mentally tortured and it is alleged that her mother in law did not give her food for three to four days continuously and the mother in law along with other other relatives forcefully evicted her from the matrimonial home on 14.6.2023 and she was told that unless she brings Rs.50 lakhs in dowry she would not be allowed to reside in her matrimonial home.
The statement of the complainant and other relatives were recorded before the trial courts where she has supported the contents of the complaint.

4. The trial court after considering the entire facts and circumstances which are mentioned above and also considering that the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution, issued summons to the petitioners.

5. The petitioners approached this Court assailing the summoning order and prayed that there was likelihood of the dispute being settled through the process of mediation and accordingly the matter was referred to Mediation and Conciliation of this Court where no agreement could be arrived at.
6.

Learned counsel for the petitioners while assailing the impugned order has submitted that as per the averments made under Sections 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C. and also considering the fact that it was mandatory to have the matter inquired by the police and by not doing so he has violated the mandatory provisions of Section 202 Cr.P.C. and accordingly the impugned order is illegal, arbitrary and deserves to be set a side.

In support of his submissions he has relied upon the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of Abhijit Pawar Vs. Hemant Madhukar Nimbalkar and another, (2017) 3 Supreme Court Cases 528.
7.

entities.text: Abhijit Pawar Vs. Hemant Madhukar Nimbalkar and another, (2017) 3 Supreme Court Cases 528
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, has opposed the petition.

He submtis that at the stage of issuing summons the trial court has to see only the contents of application under Section 528 Cr.P.C. and being prima facie satisfied with regard to occurrence of cognizance offence and as per the satisfaction arrived at from perusal of the record which at this stage is only a matter of complaint and the stand of the witnesses recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that it is not mandatory under Section 202 Cr.P.C. to refer the matter for investigation by the police and what is necessary is the satisfaction arrived at by the Magistrate concerned before summoning an accused.
8. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. The only issue raised by this Court is as to whether it was mandatory for the Magistrate to have the matter inquired by the police as per the provisions of Section 202 Cr.P.C. before recording his satisfaction and issuing summons to the accused.

2 10.
We have gone through the judgment in the case of Abhijit (supra) and find that even Supreme Court has held as to what is the initial satisfaction to be arrived at by the Magistrate.

After considering all the material on record the findings of Supreme Court is recorded in paragraph 26 is as under:-
24) The requirement of conducting enquiry or directing investigation before issuing process is, therefore, not an empty formality.

What kind of 'enquiry' is needed under this provision has also been explained in Vijay Dhanuka8 case, which is reproduced hereunder:
?14.

In view of our answer to the aforesaid question, the next question which falls for our determination is whether the learned Magistrate before issuing summons has held the inquiry as mandated under Section 202 of the Code.

The word ?inquiry? has been defined under Section 2( g) of the Code, the same reads as follows:
?2. (g) ?inquiry? means every inquiry, other than a trial, conducted under this Code by a Magistrate or court;?
It is evident from the aforesaid provision, every inquiry other than a trial conducted by the Magistrate or the court is an inquiry.
No specific mode or manner of inquiry is provided under Section 202 of the Code.

In the inquiry envisaged under Section 202 of the Code, the witnesses are examined whereas under Section 200 of the Code, examination of the complainant only is necessary with the option of examining the witnesses present, if any.

This exercise by the Magistrate, for the purpose of deciding whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, is nothing but an inquiry envisaged under Section 202 of the Code.?
11. Accordingly, this Court is of the considered view that even where Magistrate issues a process he can conduct inquiry himself or have the same conducted by the police.

Once he exercises as per Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. he is deemed to have conducted inquiry which he can legally do as per Section 202 Cr.P.C. and by means of the impugned order it is evident that he has considered entire facts prior to issuance of summons to the petitioners.

Accordingly, we do not find any infirmity in the procedure followed by the Magistrate and we find that he has inquired the matter himself while considering and recording statement sunder Sections 202 Cr.P.C.
12.
For the aforesaid reasons, we do not find any infirmity either in the procedure followed or in the satisfaction recorded by him while issuing the summons.
Accordingly, the petition is bereft of merits and is accordingly dismissed.

(Alok Mathur, J.) Order Date :- 28.5.2025 RKM.
